### Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The T-GM (Telecom Grandmaster) node failed to achieve GNSS/GPS lock (ts2phc never reached LOCKED state, clock class stuck at 248/FREERUN), collapsing the entire PTP timing chain and causing all 11 downstream BC and slave sync tests to fail; a concurrent test-code bug in the pmc fallback path masked the underlying error for 3 of those tests with spurious "bad command" output.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: T-GM GNSS lock failure → full timing chain collapse** (affects: ALL 11 tests — Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority, Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, PTP metric is present verifies on slave, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, The slave node network interface is taken down and up, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

  - **Evidence:**
    - TGM suite (same job, same lab): `"Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM / Expected <bool>: false to be true"` (4 separate tgm tests)
    - TGM suite: `"Expected ts2phc clock state to be 1 for GM"` and `"Expected phc2sys to be 1 for GM"` — ts2phc (GPS→PHC) and phc2sys never reached running/locked state on the GM node `cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com`
    - dualnicbc: `"Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config / Expected <int>: 248 to equal <int>: 6"` — the BC slave sees FREERUN (248) not LOCKED (6)
    - dualnicbc: `"Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM / Expected <bool>: false to be true"` (repeated in BC outage recovery and event-enabled tests)
    - dualnicbc metric evidence: `cne_events_received{status="failed",type=".../sync/ptp-status/clock-class"}` in the "PTP metric is present verifies on slave" failure
    - dualnicbc event consumer: `"error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded"` — consumer stalls because no clock-state events are being emitted (clock never locks)
    - dualnicbc port-role evidence: `"incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)"` — with no upstream GM, the BC slave port defaults to MASTER

  - **Root Cause:** The GNSS/GPS timing source on the test-lab T-GM node (`cnfdf32`) was unavailable, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to PHC hardware clock. Because the GM clock class never dropped to 6 (LOCKED), all downstream BC and OC clocks running on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` could not enter SLAVE state. This cascaded to every dualnicbc test, which all assume a locked timing source before running. The failure is visible in every test suite in this job run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm — all suites show the same `clock class 248/FREERUN` pattern).

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Unknown — this is an infra/lab condition (GPS signal loss), not a code change. No code change can be implicated; `release-5.0` images are built from `git clone --single-branch --branch release-5.0 https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator.git` (confirmed in `build-log.txt` line 309) and deployed successfully.

  - **Is it a flake?** Yes — GPS/GNSS signal loss in the telco5gran lab (`rdu2.redhat.com`) is a known intermittent condition. It is not reproducible by code change and should resolve on the next run when the signal is restored.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Retry the job. If the failure recurs, file a lab-infra ticket to investigate the GNSS antenna/receiver on `cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com`. Consider adding a preflight check that asserts `ts2phc` LOCKED state before any sync-dependent tests begin.

---

- **Group 2: Broken pmc fallback in test code — `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` passed as separate argv entries** (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority — those 3 where pmc fallback was reached)

  - **Evidence:**
    - `"parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Slave can sync to master, at `ptptesthelper.go:71`)
    - `"grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Downstream slave can sync to BC master, at `ptp.go:903`)
    - `"parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.0.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Can provide a profile with higher priority, at `ptptesthelper.go:71`)
    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `3b93c9f4` ("tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups", June 9 2026, author `nocturnalastro`, merged on `main`) introduced `getClockIDViaPMC` as a fallback when ptp4l log parsing fails. The function calls pmc via `ExecCommand` with `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` as two separate slice entries. In linuxptp's pmc, each positional argument after options is treated as a full management command string (e.g., `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`); splitting them causes pmc to reject both tokens with `"bad command"`. The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`. This bug lives entirely in test code on `main`; it does not require a `release-5.0` cherry-pick because tests always run from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main` confirmed in build log line 37).

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `3b93c9f4` — "tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups" — [`openshift/ptp-operator` main](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator) (June 9 2026). Not a `release-5.0` code change; test scripts are `main`-only. No backport needed.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** infra_other (primary — GNSS lock failure); test_regression (secondary — broken pmc argv in `getClockIDViaPMC`)

**Suite Severity:** HIGH — the infra failure caused 11/11 dualnicbc tests to fail (plus matching failures across every other suite in the same job); the test-code regression is independently MEDIUM and will recur on any run where log parsing falls back to pmc.

  - **Root Cause:** `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:580–613` — "Slave can sync to master" calls `ptptesthelper.BasicClockSyncCheck(...)` twice for DualNIC modes (primary and then `fullConfig.DiscoveredClockUnderTestSecondaryPtpConfig`). All subsequent serial tests that depend on a locked DualNIC clock state (clockClass, metrics, outage recovery, phc2sys HA failover) then cascade-fail because the PTP baseline was never established. Single-NIC BC (`bc`) passes because it skips the secondary check. Both `dualnicbc` and `dualnicbcha` share this exact failure topology, pointing to a common underlying cause in the DualNIC hardware path rather than the HA-specific logic. The most likely upstream cause is either a hardware connectivity issue with the secondary NIC in the telco lab (cnfdf30/cnfdf31/cnfdf32, `6.12.0-211.39.1.el10_2.x86_64`) or a regression in the `release-5.0` linuxptp-daemon image that prevents secondary NIC PTP synchronization.

Test code changes on `main` (`d20ffcbf`, `d2738968`) are only on `main` and cannot be the root cause per BRANCH AWARENESS rules (neither has been cherry-picked to `release-5.0`).

However, the parallel failure of tgm/tbc/dualfollower suites in the same job implies widespread instability rather than a simple one-off flake.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Retry the job to rule out a transient hardware outage on the secondary NIC. If the failure reproduces, inspect `linuxptp-daemon release-5.0` logs from the pod on the DualNIC node for the secondary ptp4l instance startup and sync messages. Cherry-pick relevant fixes from `main` to `release-5.0` if a daemon regression is confirmed.

- **Group 2: Event infrastructure broken — PTP Slave Clock Sync** (affects: "[dualnicbcha-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
  - **Evidence:**
    - `junit-failures.txt`: Every parallel suite fails with the identical test: `[bc-parallel]`, `[dualfollower-parallel]`, `[dualnicbc-parallel]`, `[dualnicbcha-parallel]`, `[oc-parallel]` — all with `result: error`.
    - `parallel_suite_test.go:113`: `Expect(fullConfig.Status).To(Equal(testconfig.DiscoverySuccessStatus), "parallel suite requires successful PTP discovery")` — triggered when `GetFullDiscoveredConfig` does not return `DiscoverySuccessStatus`.

The cross-suite failure (bc, dualfollower, oc parallel tests also failing) suggests the event consumer app (`parallel_suite_test.go:83`) may also have had setup issues related to the overall lab state during this run.

### Suite: oc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single OC-parallel test — `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` — failed with `result: error` because the PTP event consumer infrastructure could not deliver the required `OsClockSyncStateChange` initial event, a failure pattern shared identically across every parallel test mode in this run.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: PTP event consumer not delivering `CurrentState` events** (affects: `[It] [oc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    - `junit-failures.txt` line 70–71: `Test: [It] [oc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync / Message: result: error`
    - The identical failure appears for `bc-parallel`, `dualfollower-parallel`, `dualnicbc-parallel`, `dualnicbcha-parallel` — all five parallel modes fail on the same test with `result: error`
    - `test_results.json` header: `"fail": 0, "error": 36` — all failing tests are classified as `error`, consistent with infrastructure-level failures (not assertion failures)
    - `investigation-summary.txt`: `Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84`
    - `ci-operator-build-log.txt` line 145: `{"component":"entrypoint","error":"wrapped process failed: exit status 1","file":"sigs.k8s.io/prow/pkg/entrypoint/run.go:84","func":"sigs.k8s.io/prow/pkg/entrypoint.Options.internalRun","level":"error","msg":"Error executing test process","severity":"error","time":"2026-07-29T05:28:01Z"}`
  - **Root Cause:** In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` the `testSyncState()` function calls `event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)` up to 30 times; each attempt streams consumer pod logs looking for the regex `Got CurrentState: ({.*})`. That log is emitted in `examples/consumer/main.go:294` only when the cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` HTTP endpoint returns `200 OK` — if the endpoint is absent, errors, or returns no event JSON, the debug line is never printed. Because this failure reproduces identically in every parallel mode (oc, bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha), the shared consumer-creation path in `parallel_suite_test.go` around line 90 (`event.CreateConsumerApp`) or the cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` handler itself is the broken component. The most likely immediate cause is that the cloud-event-proxy images shipped in the `5.0.0-0.nightly-2026-07-23-224236` OCP payload (which pre-populated the internal registry before the test ran) include `redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy` PR [#717](https://github.com/redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy/pull/717) ("OCPBUGS-90708: fix CurrentState aggregation", merged Jul 6), which changed the `CurrentState` API handler to filter out non-chronyd entries when chronyd is active — potentially returning an empty or 404 response for PTP `OsClockSyncStateChange` in certain clock modes, preventing the consumer from logging the required `Got CurrentState:` line.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** [redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy#717](https://github.com/redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy/pull/717) — "OCPBUGS-90708: fix CurrentState aggregation" (merged 2026-07-06, present in Jul 23 nightly). Alternatively a transient consumer-pod startup failure (see flake note). Branch-awareness check: this change is in `redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy` main; its backport status to `release-5.0` of `openshift/cloud-event-proxy` has not been confirmed and should be verified with `python scripts/check_backport.py /tmp/ci-investigate <sha> release-5.0`.
  - **Is it a flake?** Possibly — the investigation-summary explicitly says "Check if this is a flake (retry the job) or a real regression from a recent commit." However, the failure is highly consistent (every parallel mode fails on the identical test), which argues against a transient flake and toward a deterministic regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Verify whether `redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy` PR #717's `CurrentState` filtering logic returns a non-200 response (or an empty body) for PTP `OsClockSyncStateChange` when chronyd is not active for OC/BC modes; if so, the fix is to ensure the endpoint always returns a valid event JSON (or restore the previous aggregation logic for non-chronyd profiles) so that `examples/consumer/main.go:294` logs `Got CurrentState:` and `PushInitialEvent` can succeed. **Root Cause Groups:**

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** Two independent failures — a GNSS hardware meltdown on cnfdf32 and a test-code event-key regression — account for 35 of 36 failures; one tbc test is a flake.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. This is an **infrastructure failure**, not a code regression.

- **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (2026-07-03, "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines 742–751 to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full `ResourceAddress`, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415` was never updated and still reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, which are always nil under the new scheme. The clock IS actually locked (raw event shows `"value":"LOCKED"`), but `wasLocked` never becomes `true`, so every parallel suite's `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` times out after 5 minutes. The oc suite additionally shows symptoms consistent with a cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` API change (PR #717) affecting initial-event delivery, but the key-mismatch regression is the dominant shared cause.

- **1/36 failures — TBC `BeforeEach` discovery flake** (suite: tbc)
  The `PTP Reboot discovery` `BeforeEach` in `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go` asserts `DiscoveredClockUnderTestPtpConfig != nil` before reaching the hardcoded `Skip("This is covered by QE")`; for the TBC mode the discovery assertion threw first, turning a skip into an error. The identical test correctly skipped in every other hardware mode in the same run. No relevant commits to `main` or `release-5.0` in the 13 days before the run; this is transient infrastructure stress on the TBC node.

1. **Fix the event-values key mismatch in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415`** — update `testSyncState()` to look up event values by `ResourceAddress` key (matching the new scheme in `event.go`), or iterate the map to find the string-typed entry for the `notification` state instead of using the hard-coded `"notification"` key. ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression  
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `3b93c9f4` ("tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups", June 9 2026, author `nocturnalastro`, merged on `main`) introduced `getClockIDViaPMC` as a fallback when ptp4l log parsing fails. The function calls pmc via `ExecCommand` with `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` as two separate slice entries. In linuxptp's pmc, each positional argument after options is treated as a full management command string (e.g., `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`); splitting them causes pmc to reject both tokens with `"bad command"`. The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`. This bug lives entirely in test code on `main`; it does not require a `release-5.0` cherry-pick because tests always run from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main` confirmed in build log line 37).

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `3b93c9f4` — "tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups" — [`openshift/ptp-operator` main](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator) (June 9 2026). Not a `release-5.0` code change; test scripts are `main`-only. No backport needed.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** infra_other (primary — GNSS lock failure); test_regression (secondary — broken pmc argv in `getClockIDViaPMC`)

**Suite Severity:** HIGH — the infra failure caused 11/11 dualnicbc tests to fail (plus matching failures across every other suite in the same job); the test-code regression is independently MEDIUM and will recur on any run where log parsing falls back to pmc.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** Two independent failures — a GNSS hardware meltdown on cnfdf32 and a test-code event-key regression — account for 35 of 36 failures; one tbc test is a flake.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. This is an **infrastructure failure**, not a code regression.

- **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (2026-07-03, "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines 742–751 to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full `ResourceAddress`, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415` was never updated and still reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, which are always nil under the new scheme. The clock IS actually locked (raw event shows `"value":"LOCKED"`), but `wasLocked` never becomes `true`, so every parallel suite's `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` times out after 5 minutes. The oc suite additionally shows symptoms consistent with a cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` API change (PR #717) affecting initial-event delivery, but the key-mismatch regression is the dominant shared cause.

- **1/36 failures — TBC `BeforeEach` discovery flake** (suite: tbc)
  The `PTP Reboot discovery` `BeforeEach` in `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go` asserts `DiscoveredClockUnderTestPtpConfig != nil` before reaching the hardcoded `Skip("This is covered by QE")`; for the TBC mode the discovery assertion threw first, turning a skip into an error. The identical test correctly skipped in every other hardware mode in the same run. No relevant commits to `main` or `release-5.0` in the 13 days before the run; this is transient infrastructure stress on the TBC node.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression  
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`.   - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

---

- **Group 2: Broken pmc fallback in test code — `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` passed as separate argv entries** (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority — those 3 where pmc fallback was reached)

  - **Evidence:**
    - `"parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Slave can sync to master, at `ptptesthelper.go:71`)
    - `"grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Downstream slave can sync to BC master, at `ptp.go:903`)
    - `"parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.0.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Can provide a profile with higher priority, at `ptptesthelper.go:71`)
    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `3b93c9f4` ("tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups", June 9 2026, author `nocturnalastro`, merged on `main`) introduced `getClockIDViaPMC` as a fallback when ptp4l log parsing fails. The function calls pmc via `ExecCommand` with `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` as two separate slice entries. In linuxptp's pmc, each positional argument after options is treated as a full management command string (e.g., `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`); splitting them causes pmc to reject both tokens with `"bad command"`. The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`. This bug lives entirely in test code on `main`; it does not require a `release-5.0` cherry-pick because tests always run from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main` confirmed in build log line 37).

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `3b93c9f4` — "tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups" — [`openshift/ptp-operator` main](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator) (June 9 2026). Not a `release-5.0` code change; test scripts are `main`-only. No backport needed.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. - **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression  
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `3b93c9f4` ("tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups", June 9 2026, author `nocturnalastro`, merged on `main`) introduced `getClockIDViaPMC` as a fallback when ptp4l log parsing fails. The function calls pmc via `ExecCommand` with `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` as two separate slice entries. In linuxptp's pmc, each positional argument after options is treated as a full management command string (e.g., `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`); splitting them causes pmc to reject both tokens with `"bad command"`. The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`. This bug lives entirely in test code on `main`; it does not require a `release-5.0` cherry-pick because tests always run from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main` confirmed in build log line 37).

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. This is an **infrastructure failure**, not a code regression.

- **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (2026-07-03, "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines 742–751 to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full `ResourceAddress`, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415` was never updated and still reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, which are always nil under the new scheme. The clock IS actually locked (raw event shows `"value":"LOCKED"`), but `wasLocked` never becomes `true`, so every parallel suite's `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` times out after 5 minutes. The oc suite additionally shows symptoms consistent with a cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` API change (PR #717) affecting initial-event delivery, but the key-mismatch regression is the dominant shared cause.

- **1/36 failures — TBC `BeforeEach` discovery flake** (suite: tbc)
  The `PTP Reboot discovery` `BeforeEach` in `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go` asserts `DiscoveredClockUnderTestPtpConfig != nil` before reaching the hardcoded `Skip("This is covered by QE")`; for the TBC mode the discovery assertion threw first, turning a skip into an error. The identical test correctly skipped in every other hardware mode in the same run. No relevant commits to `main` or `release-5.0` in the 13 days before the run; this is transient infrastructure stress on the TBC node.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression  
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** Two independent failures — a GNSS hardware meltdown on cnfdf32 and a test-code event-key regression — account for 35 of 36 failures; one tbc test is a flake.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. This is an **infrastructure failure**, not a code regression.

- **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (2026-07-03, "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines 742–751 to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full `ResourceAddress`, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415` was never updated and still reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, which are always nil under the new scheme. The clock IS actually locked (raw event shows `"value":"LOCKED"`), but `wasLocked` never becomes `true`, so every parallel suite's `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` times out after 5 minutes. The oc suite additionally shows symptoms consistent with a cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` API change (PR #717) affecting initial-event delivery, but the key-mismatch regression is the dominant shared cause.

- **1/36 failures — TBC `BeforeEach` discovery flake** (suite: tbc)
  The `PTP Reboot discovery` `BeforeEach` in `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go` asserts `DiscoveredClockUnderTestPtpConfig != nil` before reaching the hardcoded `Skip("This is covered by QE")`; for the TBC mode the discovery assertion threw first, turning a skip into an error. The identical test correctly skipped in every other hardware mode in the same run. No relevant commits to `main` or `release-5.0` in the 13 days before the run; this is transient infrastructure stress on the TBC node.

---

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Fix the event-values key mismatch in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415`** — update `testSyncState()` to look up event values by `ResourceAddress` key (matching the new scheme in `event.go`), or iterate the map to find the string-typed entry for the `notification` state instead of using the hard-coded `"notification"` key. This unblocks all 5 parallel suite tests deterministically and requires no infra changes.

2. **Investigate and remediate the GNSS/gpsd instability on `cnfdf32`** — with `gpsd` crashing 363 times in a single run, the lab hardware or driver configuration is fundamentally unhealthy. File a lab issue to restart/replace the GNSS receiver, recheck `gpsd` version compatibility with the kernel (`6.12.0-211.39.1.el10_2.x86_64`), and add a pre-flight check that aborts tgm/dualnicbc/dualnicbcha suites immediately if `ts2phc` is not LOCKED within a timeout, rather than letting 30 tests cascade-fail.

3. **Guard the TBC `BeforeEach` against discovery failure before the hardcoded `Skip`** — add an explicit `if fullConfig.DiscoveredClockUnderTestPtpConfig == nil { Skip("TBC config not discovered") }` guard at the top of the `PTP Reboot discovery` `BeforeEach`, so infrastructure discovery failures produce a skip rather than an error and do not pollute failure counts.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression  
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

    - `"parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.0.config: bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (test: Can provide a profile with higher priority, at `ptptesthelper.go:71`)
    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `3b93c9f4` ("tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups", June 9 2026, author `nocturnalastro`, merged on `main`) introduced `getClockIDViaPMC` as a fallback when ptp4l log parsing fails. In linuxptp's pmc, each positional argument after options is treated as a full management command string (e.g., `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`); splitting them causes pmc to reject both tokens with `"bad command"`. The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`. This bug lives entirely in test code on `main`; it does not require a `release-5.0` cherry-pick because tests always run from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main` confirmed in build log line 37).

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

    - Source: `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:144–151` — function `getClockIDViaPMC` introduced in commit `3b93c9f4`:
      ```go
      buf, _, err := pods.ExecCommand(client.Client, true, pod,
          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `3b93c9f4` ("tests: add retries to PTP clock ID lookups", June 9 2026, author `nocturnalastro`, merged on `main`) introduced `getClockIDViaPMC` as a fallback when ptp4l log parsing fails. The function calls pmc via `ExecCommand` with `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` as two separate slice entries. In linuxptp's pmc, each positional argument after options is treated as a full management command string (e.g., `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"`); splitting them causes pmc to reject both tokens with `"bad command"`. The fix is to merge them into a single string: `[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}`. This bug lives entirely in test code on `main`; it does not require a `release-5.0` cherry-pick because tests always run from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main` confirmed in build log line 37).

  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic test-code regression. Whenever pmc fallback is triggered (log parsing misses a sync message), the broken argv format causes `"bad command"` and the test times out. It will reproduce on every run where the primary log-based lookup fails.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go` `getClockIDViaPMC`, change `"GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"` to the single string `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` in the `ExecCommand` slice so pmc receives it as one management command.

**Suite Severity:** HIGH — the infra failure caused 11/11 dualnicbc tests to fail (plus matching failures across every other suite in the same job); the test-code regression is independently MEDIUM and will recur on any run where log parsing falls back to pmc.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** Two independent failures — a GNSS hardware meltdown on cnfdf32 and a test-code event-key regression — account for 35 of 36 failures; one tbc test is a flake.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. This is an **infrastructure failure**, not a code regression.

- **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (2026-07-03, "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines 742–751 to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full `ResourceAddress`, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel test failed because a July 3 commit changed the event-value key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` without updating the consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`, causing `OsClockSyncStateChange` events to be silently mis-parsed so the clock is never recorded as LOCKED.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key mismatch — event.go uses ResourceAddress, test reads DataType keys** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-josTX/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    ```
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 05:03:41.826616136 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:2]]
    DEBUG [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    ```
    The event data from the daemon clearly shows `value:"LOCKED"` and `value:"2"` for two values sharing ResourceAddress `/cluster/node/cnfdf32.../CLOCK_REALTIME`. The StoredEventValues map ends up as `map["/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME": 2]` — the LOCKED notification is overwritten by the metric.
    
    In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` lines 413–414 (main branch):
    ```go
    state, _       := values["notification"].(string)   // nil — key does not exist
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)        // 0.0 — key does not exist
    ```
    Since `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and after the 5-minute `tcEndChan` fires (at `ptp.go:393`), the test fails with "OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out".

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cec` (2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~744–749 to use `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)`, to fix a collision for BC-mode clock-class events that have two `"metric"` values. However, `OsClockSyncStateChange` events have TWO values with the **same** ResourceAddress but different DataTypes (`notification`/`metric`); using ResourceAddress as key causes the `"LOCKED"` string from the notification entry to be overwritten by the numeric metric value `2`. `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` was not updated and still reads the old `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys, so both lookups return nil and `wasLocked` stays false permanently.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" merged 2026-07-03. The commit changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (and other parallel test consumers) using the old key names. The `scripts/check_backport.py` script was not present in the workspace; however, inspection of the `release-5.0` branch of `event.go` shows it also contains the same `v.Resource` keying change, confirming the commit was merged to both branches, but `parallel/ptp.go` was not updated on either branch.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The key mismatch is deterministic: `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` will always be nil under the new scheme.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` (all `OsClockSyncStateChange` event consumers) to look up the ResourceAddress key (e.g., iterate over the `values` map to find the entry whose underlying type is string for `state`, and float64 for `clockOffset`), or alternatively add a secondary index in `event.go` that stores both the ResourceAddress key AND the DataType key so legacy consumers continue to work.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression  
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

          pkg.PtpContainerName, []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"})
      ```
      `"GET"` and `"PARENT_DATA_SET"` are separate argv elements; pmc (linuxptp) processes each remaining argument as an independent command string and rejects both — `"bad command: GET"` (GET without a TLV name) and `"bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET"` (TLV name without an action).

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

## Root Cause Groups

- **30/36 failures — GNSS hardware instability on cnfdf32 → full timing chain collapse** (suites: tgm, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  `gpsd` crash-looped 363 times on the WPC GM node `cnfdf32`, preventing `ts2phc` from converting GPS signal to a locked PHC clock (`ts2phc` state stayed `FREERUN`, clock class 248). With no locked grandmaster, every downstream BC and OC slave on `cnfdf30`/`cnfdf31` defaulted to MASTER/FAULTY port roles, collapsing all tgm serial tests (11) and all dualnicbc (10) and dualnicbcha (9) serial tests that depend on a locked upstream timing source. This is an **infrastructure failure**, not a code regression.

- **5/36 failures — Event-values key mismatch in `event.go` breaks all parallel `PTP Slave Clock Sync` tests** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (2026-07-03, "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` lines 742–751 to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full `ResourceAddress`, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:414–415` was never updated and still reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, which are always nil under the new scheme. The clock IS actually locked (raw event shows `"value":"LOCKED"`), but `wasLocked` never becomes `true`, so every parallel suite's `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` times out after 5 minutes. The oc suite additionally shows symptoms consistent with a cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` API change (PR #717) affecting initial-event delivery, but the key-mismatch regression is the dominant shared cause.

- **1/36 failures — TBC `BeforeEach` discovery flake** (suite: tbc)
  The `PTP Reboot discovery` `BeforeEach` in `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go` asserts `DiscoveredClockUnderTestPtpConfig != nil` before reaching the hardcoded `Skip("This is covered by QE")`; for the TBC mode the discovery assertion threw first, turning a skip into an error. The identical test correctly skipped in every other hardware mode in the same run. No relevant commits to `main` or `release-5.0` in the 13 days before the run; this is transient infrastructure stress on the TBC node.
