---

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.

---

## Cross-Suite Patterns

| Root Cause | bc | dualfollower | dualnicbc | dualnicbcha | tbc | all | tgm | Suite-specific? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| StoredEventValues key mismatch (`d20ffcbf`) | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | — | — | No — affects all parallel OS-clock-sync consumers |
| pmc `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` rejection (PR #629) | — | — | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | No — lab-wide; both BC suites affected identically |
| T-BC hardware topology absent (PR #205) | — | — | — | — | ✓ | ✓ | — | No — same BeforeSuite failure seen in both suites |
| ts2phc FREERUN / `--servo_num_offset_values` (PR #629) | — | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ | Yes — T-GM hardware path only |

> **Note:** PR #629 (`14eb788`) contributes to two distinct root causes: the pmc invocation bug (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) and the ts2phc servo parameter regression (tgm).

---

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix pmc invocation in linuxptp-daemon PR #629** — This single commit is responsible for 21 of 36 failures across dualnicbc and dualnicbcha. In `pkg/pmc/pmc.go:RunPMCGetParentDS` (around line 294), split `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` into two arguments (`"GET"`, `"PARENT_DATA_SET"`) when calling `exec.Command`, matching how pmc actually parses interactive-mode commands. Verify fix against both `main` and `release-5.0`; if `14eb788` has already been cherry-picked to `release-5.0`, backport the fix there too.

2. **Fix `createStoredEvent` key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (commit `d20ffcbf`)** — Use a composite key `v.Resource + ":" + string(v.DataType)` instead of `v.Resource` alone to prevent the metric entry from overwriting the notification entry for `OsClockSyncStateChange` events. Additionally update `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:verifyEvent` and `verifyMetric` to use the same composite key, since they carry the same stale assumption.

3. **Guard T-BC suite setup against missing hardware, or provision WPC NIC in the lab** — In `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, change `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` to call `Skip()` (not fail) when `len(*data.solutions["TBC"]) == 0`, so the suite degrades gracefully on labs without the required Intel E810-XXV-4T topology. Longer-term, add a WPC NIC node to the `periodic-ci…nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream` pool to make T-BC tests actually exercisable. Also lower or make configurable the `--servo_num_offset_values` default (currently 10) injected by PR #629 in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1136` to unblock the T-GM suite on E830 hardware.

Alternatively, gate the injection of `--servo_offset_threshold` / `--servo_num_offset_values` so that they are only added when the hardware supports tight convergence (e.g., only when `frequencyTraceable=true`).

---

- **Group 2: Log-stream context deadline exceeded — expected events/logs never appear** (affects: "Should check for ptp events"; "Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on logs")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    PTP event was not generated in the pod linuxptp-daemon-l95vg, err=could not find regex in log stream
    for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-l95vg container=cloud-event-proxy,
    err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    
    error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer:
    context deadline exceeded
    
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
    container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** These timeouts are a direct cascade from Group 1. Because ts2phc never reaches LOCKED, ptp4l's clock class never becomes 6, and cloud-event-proxy never publishes the LOCKED/SyncStateChange events that the test's consumer pod is waiting to read. The log-stream deadline (context deadline exceeded) fires before the expected regex patterns appear. The new `liveGate` mechanism introduced in PR #629 (`pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 376–424, `pkg/daemon/ready.go`) also adds up to a 60-second delay before `processStatus UP` is sent, potentially compressing event replay windows.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — caused by the same deterministic Group 1 regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1 (ts2phc LOCKED regression). No independent fix is needed for these tests once the GM achieves LOCKED.

---

- **Group 3: phc2sys does not return to status=1 after SIGTERM** (affects: "Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM")
  - **Evidence:**

    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0 to equal <string>: 1
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** phc2sys is killed with SIGTERM and is expected to restart and achieve `ProcessStatus=1` (UP+LOCKED) within 180s. Because the T-GM is stuck in FREERUN (Group 1), phc2sys restarts but cannot achieve a LOCKED clock state, so the metric stays 0. Additionally, PR #629 restructured process startup to use `runSocketWriter` + `liveGate` (`daemon.go` lines 1810–1877); `processStatus UP` is now sent only after dialing the event socket AND waiting for the live gate — adding a potential ~60s window. Both factors together prevent phc2sys from being declared UP within the 180s test timeout.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — directly caused by Group 1 plus the new socket-writer timing constraints.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1. Separately, ensure the `liveGate` timeout path (currently 60s) does not delay individual process restart status reports after the daemon is already running.

---

- **Group 4: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` Prometheus counter reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: "Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```

    Expected <int>: 4 to be >= <int>: 7
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go` line 58, `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics`:
    ```go
    ProcessRestartCount.Delete(prometheus.Labels{"process": process, "node": NodeName, "config": config})
    ```
    `ProcessRestartCount` is a `prometheus.CounterVec` (`pkg/metrics/register.go` line 93). Calling `Delete()` on a Counter label removes it from the Prometheus registry; when the same label set is later incremented, Prometheus starts it at 0. The test records an initial count of 7, deletes the PtpConfig (which calls `DeleteMetrics` → `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` → counter deleted), re-applies the config (ts2phc restarts 4 more times → counter=4), and then asserts count ≥ 7. It gets 4 because the counter was zeroed. This is an independent code bug introduced in PR #629's cleanup refactor.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic counter reset.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove `ProcessRestartCount.Delete()` from `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go`. Prometheus Counters are intended to be monotonically increasing for the lifetime of the process; only `ProcessStatus` (a Gauge) should be deleted on config removal.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix pmc invocation in linuxptp-daemon PR #629** — This single commit is responsible for 21 of 36 failures across dualnicbc and dualnicbcha. In `pkg/pmc/pmc.go:RunPMCGetParentDS` (around line 294), split `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` into two arguments (`"GET"`, `"PARENT_DATA_SET"`) when calling `exec.Command`, matching how pmc actually parses interactive-mode commands. Also lower or make configurable the `--servo_num_offset_values` default (currently 10) injected by PR #629 in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1136` to unblock the T-GM suite on E830 hardware.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The BC parallel OS-clock-sync test always timed out because commit `d20ffcbf` changed the event-value key strategy in `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `parallel/ptp.go` using the old key format, so every received `LOCKED` event was silently ignored.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Event-value key format mismatch in `testSyncState()`** (affects: `[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][event.go: 730] ... "value":"LOCKED" ... "value":"-18"
    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [Jul 29 09:49:39.666][event.go: 589] received term signal, exiting MonitorPodLogsRegex
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw CloudEvent data contained `"value":"LOCKED"` at 09:44:44 — 9 seconds into the test — yet the test ran to its full 5-minute timeout. `clockOffset=0.000000` proves the `values["metric"].(float64)` assertion returned the zero value (key missing), confirming the key lookup was broken.

The change was made to prevent key collisions in BC-mode clock-class events where two entries share the same `DataType`. However, for `OsClockSyncStateChange` events both the notification and metric value entries share the **same** ResourceAddress, so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry in the loop, and neither `"notification"` nor `"metric"` key ends up in the map. The consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`, both return Go zero values, so `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test always fails at the timeout guard on `ptp.go:392–393`.   - **Is it a flake?** No. The hardware was correctly LOCKED (the raw event proves it); the test code structurally cannot recognise a LOCKED event with the current key format. Every run will time out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` and `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:4140,4152`, replace the `values["notification"]` / `values["metric"]` key lookups with a loop over the `StoredEventValues` map that inspects the actual value types (string → notification state, float64 → metric), or alternatively restore the old `DataType`-keyed storage for single-resource events (e.g. fall back to `DataType` key when all `Resource` fields are identical) in `event.go:747–751`.

**Root Cause Groups:**

    ```

    bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET
    ```

    bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

    incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)

In the linuxptp pmc tool, two separate "bad command" lines indicate pmc processed `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as **two separate positional arguments**, each failing individually, rather than as a single `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` command string. This regression was introduced by linuxptp-daemon commit `14eb788` ("Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", PR #629), which added `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` as a **brand-new file**. In `RunPMCGetParentDS` at line 294 of that file: `exec.Command("pmc", "-u", "-b", "0", "-f", "/var/run/"+configFileName, cmdStr)` — `cmdStr` is `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` passed as a **single argument**. Whether the issue is in this function or in how the conformance test itself invokes pmc (also cloned from `main` because `USE_UPSTREAM=true`), the result is that pmc receives the two tokens as separate commands, both fail, the daemon cannot query `PARENT_DATA_SET` from ptp4l, the BC interface `ens2f0np0` is never told to enter SLAVE role, and stays in MASTER (clock class 248). All subsequent tests — phc2sys startup, outage recovery, clock class verification, event publishing — cascade-fail because BC sync is never established. File `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` (new file, introduced in this commit). Because `USE_UPSTREAM=true`, this main-branch commit **is** in the production image for this job — no cherry-pick to `release-5.0` is needed for it to have effect here.
  - **Is it a flake?** No. The identical `bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` pattern appears in every affected test across every suite (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm, bc, dualfollower), and the BC interface consistently reads MASTER state. A flake would not produce reproducible identical error strings across 20+ tests.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` `RunPMCGetParentDS`, replace `exec.Command("pmc", ..., cmdStr)` (passing `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as one arg) with `exec.Command("pmc", "-u", "-b", "0", "-f", "/var/run/"+configFileName, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET")` — two separate positional args as pmc expects. Audit any conformance-test pmc helpers (in `ptp-operator` main) for the same pattern.

- **Group 2: Event consumer context deadline exceeded** (affects: "[dualnicbcha-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** This is a direct downstream consequence of Group 1. With the BC unable to lock (clock class 248, no upstream sync), cloud-event-proxy never publishes a `lock-state` or `clock-class` event. The `consumer` pod in `ptp-event-framework-test` namespace waits to receive an initial event and hits its read deadline because no event is ever emitted. There is no independent bug here.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Same as Group 1; fixing the pmc invocation will restore clock sync and enable event flow.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** `test_regression`

**Suite Severity:** CRITICAL — every single test in the suite fails, BC clock sync is completely broken across all suites in this job, and the root cause is a code regression shipped in the last upstream sync (7 days before this run).

## tgm

---

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** All 11 T-GM serial tests fail due to a common upstream code regression where ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite the DPLL being LOCKED, cascading into event-stream timeouts, metric anomalies, and a discrete restart-counter reset bug introduced in linuxptp-daemon PR #629.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: T-GM timing chain stuck in FREERUN — ts2phc never reaches LOCKED state** (affects: "Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics"; "Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted"; "WPC GM GNSS signal loss tests Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss"; "WPC GM ts2phc termination tests Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED"; "WPC GM Events verification (V2) Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="dpll"} 1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="ts2phc"} 0
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false to be true
    Expected phc2sys to be  1 for GM; Expected <bool>: false to be true
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `dpll=1 (LOCKED)` while `ts2phc=0 (FREERUN)` is the smoking gun: the GNSS hardware signal is present and the DPLL is locked, but ts2phc is not transitioning to LOCKED. PR #629 in linuxptp-daemon ("Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", SHA `14eb788`) dynamically injects new ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 1120–1137, including `--servo_num_offset_values 10` (requires 10 consecutive offsets within the `--servo_offset_threshold` before declaring LOCKED). When the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold` is stricter than what the hardware can achieve, ts2phc never accumulates 10 consecutive in-spec offsets and remains FREERUN, preventing ptp4l clock class from reaching 6, and phc2sys from locking. This is a test regression introduced by the upstream sync.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon [PR #629](https://github.com/openshift/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)", SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22. Backport status to `release-5.0` could not be verified (check_backport.py script absent and no `release-5.0` branch in local clone).
  - **Is it a flake?** No — 6 of 11 tests across all T-GM scenarios consistently show `ts2phc=FREERUN` and `ptp4l clockClass≠6`. This is a systemic behavioral regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` around line 1136, make `--servo_num_offset_values` configurable or lower the default from 10 to a value compatible with E830 hardware behavior. Alternatively, gate the injection of `--servo_offset_threshold` / `--servo_num_offset_values` so that they are only added when the hardware supports tight convergence (e.g., only when `frequencyTraceable=true`).

---

- **Group 2: Log-stream context deadline exceeded — expected events/logs never appear** (affects: "Should check for ptp events"; "Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on logs")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    PTP event was not generated in the pod linuxptp-daemon-l95vg, err=could not find regex in log stream
    for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-l95vg container=cloud-event-proxy,
    err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    
    error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer:
    context deadline exceeded
    
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
    container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** These timeouts are a direct cascade from Group 1. Because ts2phc never reaches LOCKED, ptp4l's clock class never becomes 6, and cloud-event-proxy never publishes the LOCKED/SyncStateChange events that the test's consumer pod is waiting to read. The log-stream deadline (context deadline exceeded) fires before the expected regex patterns appear. The new `liveGate` mechanism introduced in PR #629 (`pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 376–424, `pkg/daemon/ready.go`) also adds up to a 60-second delay before `processStatus UP` is sent, potentially compressing event replay windows.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — caused by the same deterministic Group 1 regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1 (ts2phc LOCKED regression). No independent fix is needed for these tests once the GM achieves LOCKED.

---

- **Group 3: phc2sys does not return to status=1 after SIGTERM** (affects: "Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    Timed out after 180.000s.
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0 to equal <string>: 1
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** phc2sys is killed with SIGTERM and is expected to restart and achieve `ProcessStatus=1` (UP+LOCKED) within 180s. Because the T-GM is stuck in FREERUN (Group 1), phc2sys restarts but cannot achieve a LOCKED clock state, so the metric stays 0. Additionally, PR #629 restructured process startup to use `runSocketWriter` + `liveGate` (`daemon.go` lines 1810–1877); `processStatus UP` is now sent only after dialing the event socket AND waiting for the live gate — adding a potential ~60s window. Both factors together prevent phc2sys from being declared UP within the 180s test timeout.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — directly caused by Group 1 plus the new socket-writer timing constraints.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1. Separately, ensure the `liveGate` timeout path (currently 60s) does not delay individual process restart status reports after the daemon is already running.

---

- **Group 4: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` Prometheus counter reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: "Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4 to be >= <int>: 7
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go` line 58, `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics`:
    ```go
    ProcessRestartCount.Delete(prometheus.Labels{"process": process, "node": NodeName, "config": config})
    ```
    `ProcessRestartCount` is a `prometheus.CounterVec` (`pkg/metrics/register.go` line 93). Calling `Delete()` on a Counter label removes it from the Prometheus registry; when the same label set is later incremented, Prometheus starts it at 0. The test records an initial count of 7, deletes the PtpConfig (which calls `DeleteMetrics` → `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` → counter deleted), re-applies the config (ts2phc restarts 4 more times → counter=4), and then asserts count ≥ 7. It gets 4 because the counter was zeroed. This is an independent code bug introduced in PR #629's cleanup refactor.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic counter reset.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove `ProcessRestartCount.Delete()` from `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go`. Prometheus Counters are intended to be monotonically increasing for the lifetime of the process; only `ProcessStatus` (a Gauge) should be deleted on config removal.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The BC parallel OS-clock-sync test always timed out because commit `d20ffcbf` changed the event-value key strategy in `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `parallel/ptp.go` using the old key format, so every received `LOCKED` event was silently ignored.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Event-value key format mismatch in `testSyncState()`** (affects: `[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][event.go: 730] ... "value":"LOCKED" ... "value":"-18"
    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [Jul 29 09:49:39.666][event.go: 589] received term signal, exiting MonitorPodLogsRegex
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw CloudEvent data contained `"value":"LOCKED"` at 09:44:44 — 9 seconds into the test — yet the test ran to its full 5-minute timeout. `clockOffset=0.000000` proves the `values["metric"].(float64)` assertion returned the zero value (key missing), confirming the key lookup was broken.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") refactored the V2-event parser in `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–752` to use `v.Resource` (the full ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). The change was made to prevent key collisions in BC-mode clock-class events where two entries share the same `DataType`. However, for `OsClockSyncStateChange` events both the notification and metric value entries share the **same** ResourceAddress, so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry in the loop, and neither `"notification"` nor `"metric"` key ends up in the map. The consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`, both return Go zero values, so `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test always fails at the timeout guard on `ptp.go:392–393`. The `serial/ptp.go` helper functions `verifyEvent` (line 4140) and `verifyMetric` (line 4152) have the same stale key assumptions — the commit updated `serial/ptp.go` to add new clockClass tests but did not update the existing event-value accessors in either file.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (openshift/ptp-operator `main`). The test scripts run from `main`; this commit is in `main` and directly executes in this job.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The hardware was correctly LOCKED (the raw event proves it); the test code structurally cannot recognise a LOCKED event with the current key format. Every run will time out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` and `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:4140,4152`, replace the `values["notification"]` / `values["metric"]` key lookups with a loop over the `StoredEventValues` map that inspects the actual value types (string → notification state, float64 → metric), or alternatively restore the old `DataType`-keyed storage for single-resource events (e.g. fall back to `DataType` key when all `Resource` fields are identical) in `event.go:747–751`.

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** All 11 T-GM serial tests fail due to a common upstream code regression where ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite the DPLL being LOCKED, cascading into event-stream timeouts, metric anomalies, and a discrete restart-counter reset bug introduced in linuxptp-daemon PR #629.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: T-GM timing chain stuck in FREERUN — ts2phc never reaches LOCKED state** (affects: "Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics"; "Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted"; "WPC GM GNSS signal loss tests Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss"; "WPC GM ts2phc termination tests Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED"; "WPC GM Events verification (V2) Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="dpll"} 1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="ts2phc"} 0
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false to be true
    Expected phc2sys to be  1 for GM; Expected <bool>: false to be true
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `dpll=1 (LOCKED)` while `ts2phc=0 (FREERUN)` is the smoking gun: the GNSS hardware signal is present and the DPLL is locked, but ts2phc is not transitioning to LOCKED. PR #629 in linuxptp-daemon ("Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", SHA `14eb788`) dynamically injects new ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 1120–1137, including `--servo_num_offset_values 10` (requires 10 consecutive offsets within the `--servo_offset_threshold` before declaring LOCKED). When the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold` is stricter than what the hardware can achieve, ts2phc never accumulates 10 consecutive in-spec offsets and remains FREERUN, preventing ptp4l clock class from reaching 6, and phc2sys from locking. This is a test regression introduced by the upstream sync.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon [PR #629](https://github.com/openshift/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)", SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22. Backport status to `release-5.0` could not be verified (check_backport.py script absent and no `release-5.0` branch in local clone).
  - **Is it a flake?** No — 6 of 11 tests across all T-GM scenarios consistently show `ts2phc=FREERUN` and `ptp4l clockClass≠6`. This is a systemic behavioral regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` around line 1136, make `--servo_num_offset_values` configurable or lower the default from 10 to a value compatible with E830 hardware behavior. Alternatively, gate the injection of `--servo_offset_threshold` / `--servo_num_offset_values` so that they are only added when the hardware supports tight convergence (e.g., only when `frequencyTraceable=true`).

---

- **Group 2: Log-stream context deadline exceeded — expected events/logs never appear** (affects: "Should check for ptp events"; "Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on logs")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    PTP event was not generated in the pod linuxptp-daemon-l95vg, err=could not find regex in log stream
    for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-l95vg container=cloud-event-proxy,
    err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    
    error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer:
    context deadline exceeded
    
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
    container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** These timeouts are a direct cascade from Group 1. Because ts2phc never reaches LOCKED, ptp4l's clock class never becomes 6, and cloud-event-proxy never publishes the LOCKED/SyncStateChange events that the test's consumer pod is waiting to read. The log-stream deadline (context deadline exceeded) fires before the expected regex patterns appear. The new `liveGate` mechanism introduced in PR #629 (`pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 376–424, `pkg/daemon/ready.go`) also adds up to a 60-second delay before `processStatus UP` is sent, potentially compressing event replay windows.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — caused by the same deterministic Group 1 regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1 (ts2phc LOCKED regression). No independent fix is needed for these tests once the GM achieves LOCKED.

---

- **Group 3: phc2sys does not return to status=1 after SIGTERM** (affects: "Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    Timed out after 180.000s.
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0 to equal <string>: 1
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** phc2sys is killed with SIGTERM and is expected to restart and achieve `ProcessStatus=1` (UP+LOCKED) within 180s. Because the T-GM is stuck in FREERUN (Group 1), phc2sys restarts but cannot achieve a LOCKED clock state, so the metric stays 0. Additionally, PR #629 restructured process startup to use `runSocketWriter` + `liveGate` (`daemon.go` lines 1810–1877); `processStatus UP` is now sent only after dialing the event socket AND waiting for the live gate — adding a potential ~60s window. Both factors together prevent phc2sys from being declared UP within the 180s test timeout.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — directly caused by Group 1 plus the new socket-writer timing constraints.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1. Separately, ensure the `liveGate` timeout path (currently 60s) does not delay individual process restart status reports after the daemon is already running.

---

- **Group 4: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` Prometheus counter reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: "Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4 to be >= <int>: 7
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go` line 58, `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics`:
    ```go
    ProcessRestartCount.Delete(prometheus.Labels{"process": process, "node": NodeName, "config": config})
    ```
    `ProcessRestartCount` is a `prometheus.CounterVec` (`pkg/metrics/register.go` line 93). Calling `Delete()` on a Counter label removes it from the Prometheus registry; when the same label set is later incremented, Prometheus starts it at 0. The test records an initial count of 7, deletes the PtpConfig (which calls `DeleteMetrics` → `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` → counter deleted), re-applies the config (ts2phc restarts 4 more times → counter=4), and then asserts count ≥ 7. It gets 4 because the counter was zeroed. This is an independent code bug introduced in PR #629's cleanup refactor.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic counter reset.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove `ProcessRestartCount.Delete()` from `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go`. Prometheus Counters are intended to be monotonically increasing for the lifetime of the process; only `ProcessStatus` (a Gauge) should be deleted on config removal.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix pmc invocation in linuxptp-daemon PR #629** — This single commit is responsible for 21 of 36 failures across dualnicbc and dualnicbcha. In `pkg/pmc/pmc.go:RunPMCGetParentDS` (around line 294), split `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` into two arguments (`"GET"`, `"PARENT_DATA_SET"`) when calling `exec.Command`, matching how pmc actually parses interactive-mode commands. Verify fix against both `main` and `release-5.0`; if `14eb788` has already been cherry-picked to `release-5.0`, backport the fix there too.

2. **Fix `createStoredEvent` key scheme in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (commit `d20ffcbf`)** — Use a composite key `v.Resource + ":" + string(v.DataType)` instead of `v.Resource` alone to prevent the metric entry from overwriting the notification entry for `OsClockSyncStateChange` events. Additionally update `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:verifyEvent` and `verifyMetric` to use the same composite key, since they carry the same stale assumption.

3. **Guard T-BC suite setup against missing hardware, or provision WPC NIC in the lab** — In `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, change `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` to call `Skip()` (not fail) when `len(*data.solutions["TBC"]) == 0`, so the suite degrades gracefully on labs without the required Intel E810-XXV-4T topology. Longer-term, add a WPC NIC node to the `periodic-ci…nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream` pool to make T-BC tests actually exercisable. Also lower or make configurable the `--servo_num_offset_values` default (currently 10) injected by PR #629 in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1136` to unblock the T-GM suite on E830 hardware.

- **Group 2: Log-stream context deadline exceeded — expected events/logs never appear** (affects: "Should check for ptp events"; "Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on logs")

Because ts2phc never reaches LOCKED, ptp4l's clock class never becomes 6, and cloud-event-proxy never publishes the LOCKED/SyncStateChange events that the test's consumer pod is waiting to read. The log-stream deadline (context deadline exceeded) fires before the expected regex patterns appear. The new `liveGate` mechanism introduced in PR #629 (`pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 376–424, `pkg/daemon/ready.go`) also adds up to a 60-second delay before `processStatus UP` is sent, potentially compressing event replay windows.

Additionally, PR #629 restructured process startup to use `runSocketWriter` + `liveGate` (`daemon.go` lines 1810–1877); `processStatus UP` is now sent only after dialing the event socket AND waiting for the live gate — adding a potential ~60s window.   - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — directly caused by Group 1 plus the new socket-writer timing constraints.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1. Separately, ensure the `liveGate` timeout path (currently 60s) does not delay individual process restart status reports after the daemon is already running.

- **Group 4: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` Prometheus counter reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: "Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply")

  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic counter reset.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.

- **Group 1: Event-value key format mismatch in `testSyncState()`** (affects: `[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)

    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [Jul 29 09:49:39.666][event.go: 589] received term signal, exiting MonitorPodLogsRegex

    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393

    The raw CloudEvent data contained `"value":"LOCKED"` at 09:44:44 — 9 seconds into the test — yet the test ran to its full 5-minute timeout. `clockOffset=0.000000` proves the `values["metric"].(float64)` assertion returned the zero value (key missing), confirming the key lookup was broken.

In the linuxptp pmc tool, two separate "bad command" lines indicate pmc processed `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as **two separate positional arguments**, each failing individually, rather than as a single `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` command string. This regression was introduced by linuxptp-daemon commit `14eb788` ("Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", PR #629), which added `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` as a **brand-new file**. In `RunPMCGetParentDS` at line 294 of that file: `exec.Command("pmc", "-u", "-b", "0", "-f", "/var/run/"+configFileName, cmdStr)` — `cmdStr` is `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` passed as a **single argument**. Whether the issue is in this function or in how the conformance test itself invokes pmc (also cloned from `main` because `USE_UPSTREAM=true`), the result is that pmc receives the two tokens as separate commands, both fail, the daemon cannot query `PARENT_DATA_SET` from ptp4l, the BC interface `ens2f0np0` is never told to enter SLAVE role, and stays in MASTER (clock class 248). File `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` (new file, introduced in this commit). Because `USE_UPSTREAM=true`, this main-branch commit **is** in the production image for this job — no cherry-pick to `release-5.0` is needed for it to have effect here.
  - **Is it a flake?** No. The identical `bad command: GET\nbad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` pattern appears in every affected test across every suite (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm, bc, dualfollower), and the BC interface consistently reads MASTER state. A flake would not produce reproducible identical error strings across 20+ tests.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `pkg/pmc/pmc.go` `RunPMCGetParentDS`, replace `exec.Command("pmc", ..., cmdStr)` (passing `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as one arg) with `exec.Command("pmc", "-u", "-b", "0", "-f", "/var/run/"+configFileName, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET")` — two separate positional args as pmc expects. Audit any conformance-test pmc helpers (in `ptp-operator` main) for the same pattern.

- **Group 2: Event consumer context deadline exceeded** (affects: "[dualnicbcha-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** This is a direct downstream consequence of Group 1. With the BC unable to lock (clock class 248, no upstream sync), cloud-event-proxy never publishes a `lock-state` or `clock-class` event. The `consumer` pod in `ptp-event-framework-test` namespace waits to receive an initial event and hits its read deadline because no event is ever emitted. There is no independent bug here.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Same as Group 1; fixing the pmc invocation will restore clock sync and enable event flow.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** `test_regression`

**Suite Severity:** CRITICAL — every single test in the suite fails, BC clock sync is completely broken across all suites in this job, and the root cause is a code regression shipped in the last upstream sync (7 days before this run).

## tgm

---

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** All 11 T-GM serial tests fail due to a common upstream code regression where ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite the DPLL being LOCKED, cascading into event-stream timeouts, metric anomalies, and a discrete restart-counter reset bug introduced in linuxptp-daemon PR #629.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: T-GM timing chain stuck in FREERUN — ts2phc never reaches LOCKED state** (affects: "Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics"; "Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted"; "WPC GM GNSS signal loss tests Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss"; "WPC GM ts2phc termination tests Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED"; "WPC GM Events verification (V2) Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="dpll"} 1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="ts2phc"} 0
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false to be true
    Expected phc2sys to be  1 for GM; Expected <bool>: false to be true
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `dpll=1 (LOCKED)` while `ts2phc=0 (FREERUN)` is the smoking gun: the GNSS hardware signal is present and the DPLL is locked, but ts2phc is not transitioning to LOCKED. PR #629 in linuxptp-daemon ("Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", SHA `14eb788`) dynamically injects new ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 1120–1137, including `--servo_num_offset_values 10` (requires 10 consecutive offsets within the `--servo_offset_threshold` before declaring LOCKED). When the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold` is stricter than what the hardware can achieve, ts2phc never accumulates 10 consecutive in-spec offsets and remains FREERUN, preventing ptp4l clock class from reaching 6, and phc2sys from locking. This is a test regression introduced by the upstream sync.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon [PR #629](https://github.com/openshift/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)", SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22. Backport status to `release-5.0` could not be verified (check_backport.py script absent and no `release-5.0` branch in local clone).
  - **Is it a flake?** No — 6 of 11 tests across all T-GM scenarios consistently show `ts2phc=FREERUN` and `ptp4l clockClass≠6`. This is a systemic behavioral regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` around line 1136, make `--servo_num_offset_values` configurable or lower the default from 10 to a value compatible with E830 hardware behavior. Alternatively, gate the injection of `--servo_offset_threshold` / `--servo_num_offset_values` so that they are only added when the hardware supports tight convergence (e.g., only when `frequencyTraceable=true`).

---

- **Group 2: Log-stream context deadline exceeded — expected events/logs never appear** (affects: "Should check for ptp events"; "Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on logs")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    PTP event was not generated in the pod linuxptp-daemon-l95vg, err=could not find regex in log stream
    for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-l95vg container=cloud-event-proxy,
    err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    
    error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer:
    context deadline exceeded
    
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
    container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** These timeouts are a direct cascade from Group 1. Because ts2phc never reaches LOCKED, ptp4l's clock class never becomes 6, and cloud-event-proxy never publishes the LOCKED/SyncStateChange events that the test's consumer pod is waiting to read. The log-stream deadline (context deadline exceeded) fires before the expected regex patterns appear. The new `liveGate` mechanism introduced in PR #629 (`pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 376–424, `pkg/daemon/ready.go`) also adds up to a 60-second delay before `processStatus UP` is sent, potentially compressing event replay windows.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — caused by the same deterministic Group 1 regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1 (ts2phc LOCKED regression). No independent fix is needed for these tests once the GM achieves LOCKED.

---

- **Group 3: phc2sys does not return to status=1 after SIGTERM** (affects: "Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    Timed out after 180.000s.
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0 to equal <string>: 1
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** phc2sys is killed with SIGTERM and is expected to restart and achieve `ProcessStatus=1` (UP+LOCKED) within 180s. Because the T-GM is stuck in FREERUN (Group 1), phc2sys restarts but cannot achieve a LOCKED clock state, so the metric stays 0. Additionally, PR #629 restructured process startup to use `runSocketWriter` + `liveGate` (`daemon.go` lines 1810–1877); `processStatus UP` is now sent only after dialing the event socket AND waiting for the live gate — adding a potential ~60s window. Both factors together prevent phc2sys from being declared UP within the 180s test timeout.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — directly caused by Group 1 plus the new socket-writer timing constraints.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1. Separately, ensure the `liveGate` timeout path (currently 60s) does not delay individual process restart status reports after the daemon is already running.

---

- **Group 4: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` Prometheus counter reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: "Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4 to be >= <int>: 7
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go` line 58, `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics`:
    ```go
    ProcessRestartCount.Delete(prometheus.Labels{"process": process, "node": NodeName, "config": config})
    ```
    `ProcessRestartCount` is a `prometheus.CounterVec` (`pkg/metrics/register.go` line 93). Calling `Delete()` on a Counter label removes it from the Prometheus registry; when the same label set is later incremented, Prometheus starts it at 0. The test records an initial count of 7, deletes the PtpConfig (which calls `DeleteMetrics` → `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` → counter deleted), re-applies the config (ts2phc restarts 4 more times → counter=4), and then asserts count ≥ 7. It gets 4 because the counter was zeroed. This is an independent code bug introduced in PR #629's cleanup refactor.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic counter reset.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove `ProcessRestartCount.Delete()` from `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go`. Prometheus Counters are intended to be monotonically increasing for the lifetime of the process; only `ProcessStatus` (a Gauge) should be deleted on config removal.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The BC parallel OS-clock-sync test always timed out because commit `d20ffcbf` changed the event-value key strategy in `test/pkg/event/event.go` but left `parallel/ptp.go` using the old key format, so every received `LOCKED` event was silently ignored.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Event-value key format mismatch in `testSyncState()`** (affects: `[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)

  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][event.go: 730] ... "value":"LOCKED" ... "value":"-18"
    [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [Jul 29 09:49:39.666][event.go: 589] received term signal, exiting MonitorPodLogsRegex
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw CloudEvent data contained `"value":"LOCKED"` at 09:44:44 — 9 seconds into the test — yet the test ran to its full 5-minute timeout. `clockOffset=0.000000` proves the `values["metric"].(float64)` assertion returned the zero value (key missing), confirming the key lookup was broken.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") refactored the V2-event parser in `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–752` to use `v.Resource` (the full ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `string(v.DataType)` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). The change was made to prevent key collisions in BC-mode clock-class events where two entries share the same `DataType`. However, for `OsClockSyncStateChange` events both the notification and metric value entries share the **same** ResourceAddress, so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry in the loop, and neither `"notification"` nor `"metric"` key ends up in the map. The consumer code in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`, both return Go zero values, so `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test always fails at the timeout guard on `ptp.go:392–393`. The `serial/ptp.go` helper functions `verifyEvent` (line 4140) and `verifyMetric` (line 4152) have the same stale key assumptions — the commit updated `serial/ptp.go` to add new clockClass tests but did not update the existing event-value accessors in either file.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (openshift/ptp-operator `main`). The test scripts run from `main`; this commit is in `main` and directly executes in this job.

  - **Is it a flake?** No. The hardware was correctly LOCKED (the raw event proves it); the test code structurally cannot recognise a LOCKED event with the current key format. Every run will time out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` and `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:4140,4152`, replace the `values["notification"]` / `values["metric"]` key lookups with a loop over the `StoredEventValues` map that inspects the actual value types (string → notification state, float64 → metric), or alternatively restore the old `DataType`-keyed storage for single-resource events (e.g. fall back to `DataType` key when all `Resource` fields are identical) in `event.go:747–751`.

### Suite: tgm (11 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** All 11 T-GM serial tests fail due to a common upstream code regression where ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite the DPLL being LOCKED, cascading into event-stream timeouts, metric anomalies, and a discrete restart-counter reset bug introduced in linuxptp-daemon PR #629.

---

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: T-GM timing chain stuck in FREERUN — ts2phc never reaches LOCKED state** (affects: "Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on metrics"; "Verify ts2phc clock state is not LOCKED after GM PtpConfig is deleted"; "WPC GM GNSS signal loss tests Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss"; "WPC GM ts2phc termination tests Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED"; "WPC GM Events verification (V2) Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="dpll"} 1
    openshift_ptp_clock_state{iface="ens7fx",node="cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com",process="ts2phc"} 0
    Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM
    Expected <bool>: false to be true
    Expected phc2sys to be  1 for GM; Expected <bool>: false to be true
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `dpll=1 (LOCKED)` while `ts2phc=0 (FREERUN)` is the smoking gun: the GNSS hardware signal is present and the DPLL is locked, but ts2phc is not transitioning to LOCKED. PR #629 in linuxptp-daemon ("Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", SHA `14eb788`) dynamically injects new ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 1120–1137, including `--servo_num_offset_values 10` (requires 10 consecutive offsets within the `--servo_offset_threshold` before declaring LOCKED). When the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold` is stricter than what the hardware can achieve, ts2phc never accumulates 10 consecutive in-spec offsets and remains FREERUN, preventing ptp4l clock class from reaching 6, and phc2sys from locking. This is a test regression introduced by the upstream sync.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon [PR #629](https://github.com/openshift/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629) "Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)", SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22. Backport status to `release-5.0` could not be verified (check_backport.py script absent and no `release-5.0` branch in local clone).
  - **Is it a flake?** No — 6 of 11 tests across all T-GM scenarios consistently show `ts2phc=FREERUN` and `ptp4l clockClass≠6`. This is a systemic behavioral regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` around line 1136, make `--servo_num_offset_values` configurable or lower the default from 10 to a value compatible with E830 hardware behavior. Alternatively, gate the injection of `--servo_offset_threshold` / `--servo_num_offset_values` so that they are only added when the hardware supports tight convergence (e.g., only when `frequencyTraceable=true`).

---

- **Group 2: Log-stream context deadline exceeded — expected events/logs never appear** (affects: "Should check for ptp events"; "Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart"; "WPC GM Verification Tests is verifying WPC GM state based on logs")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    PTP event was not generated in the pod linuxptp-daemon-l95vg, err=could not find regex in log stream
    for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-l95vg container=cloud-event-proxy,
    err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    
    error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer:
    context deadline exceeded
    
    could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-g64pn
    container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** These timeouts are a direct cascade from Group 1. Because ts2phc never reaches LOCKED, ptp4l's clock class never becomes 6, and cloud-event-proxy never publishes the LOCKED/SyncStateChange events that the test's consumer pod is waiting to read. The log-stream deadline (context deadline exceeded) fires before the expected regex patterns appear. The new `liveGate` mechanism introduced in PR #629 (`pkg/daemon/daemon.go` lines 376–424, `pkg/daemon/ready.go`) also adds up to a 60-second delay before `processStatus UP` is sent, potentially compressing event replay windows.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Same as Group 1 — linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — caused by the same deterministic Group 1 regression.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1 (ts2phc LOCKED regression). No independent fix is needed for these tests once the GM achieves LOCKED.

---

- **Group 3: phc2sys does not return to status=1 after SIGTERM** (affects: "Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    Timed out after 180.000s.
    Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM
    Expected <string>: 0 to equal <string>: 1
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** phc2sys is killed with SIGTERM and is expected to restart and achieve `ProcessStatus=1` (UP+LOCKED) within 180s. Because the T-GM is stuck in FREERUN (Group 1), phc2sys restarts but cannot achieve a LOCKED clock state, so the metric stays 0. Additionally, PR #629 restructured process startup to use `runSocketWriter` + `liveGate` (`daemon.go` lines 1810–1877); `processStatus UP` is now sent only after dialing the event socket AND waiting for the live gate — adding a potential ~60s window. Both factors together prevent phc2sys from being declared UP within the 180s test timeout.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — directly caused by Group 1 plus the new socket-writer timing constraints.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Fix Group 1. Separately, ensure the `liveGate` timeout path (currently 60s) does not delay individual process restart status reports after the daemon is already running.

---

- **Group 4: ts2phc `ProcessRestartCount` Prometheus counter reset on PtpConfig re-apply** (affects: "Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply")
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    ts2phc restart count should continue after re-apply (not reset), got 4 (initial was 7)
    Expected <int>: 4 to be >= <int>: 7
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go` line 58, `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics`:
    ```go
    ProcessRestartCount.Delete(prometheus.Labels{"process": process, "node": NodeName, "config": config})
    ```
    `ProcessRestartCount` is a `prometheus.CounterVec` (`pkg/metrics/register.go` line 93). Calling `Delete()` on a Counter label removes it from the Prometheus registry; when the same label set is later incremented, Prometheus starts it at 0. The test records an initial count of 7, deletes the PtpConfig (which calls `DeleteMetrics` → `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` → counter deleted), re-applies the config (ts2phc restarts 4 more times → counter=4), and then asserts count ≥ 7. It gets 4 because the counter was zeroed. This is an independent code bug introduced in PR #629's cleanup refactor.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** linuxptp-daemon PR #629, SHA `14eb788`.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — deterministic counter reset.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Remove `ProcessRestartCount.Delete()` from `DeleteProcessStatusMetrics` in `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go`. Prometheus Counters are intended to be monotonically increasing for the lifetime of the process; only `ProcessStatus` (a Gauge) should be deleted on config removal.

---

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three deterministic regressions — a `main`-branch test key-scheme bug, a linuxptp-daemon pmc invocation breakage, and missing T-BC hardware — account for all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — StoredEventValues key scheme mismatch in `createStoredEvent`** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) rather than `string(v.DataType)`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the `"notification"` and `"metric"` sub-values share the same ResourceAddress (`/CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. Consumers in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still look up `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]`, both return Go zero-values, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out every run.

- **21/36 failures — pmc rejects `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate bad commands, BC never locks** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`, merged 2026-07-22) passes `"GET PARENT_DATA_SET"` as a single `exec.Command` argument rather than two separate arguments, causing pmc to parse each token individually and print `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET`. With pmc unable to query `PARENT_DATA_SET`, the BC upstream port (`ens2f0np0`) is never transitioned to SLAVE, stays MASTER, clock class remains 248 instead of 6, and every downstream PTP assertion across both dualnicbc and dualnicbcha suites fails in cascade.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC hardware topology absent from CI lab** (suites: tbc, all)
  PR #205 (commit `aede1e93`, merged June 23 2026 to `main`) added the T-BC test suite and calls `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` from `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`. The function's `AlgoTelcoBCString` solver in `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go:1898–1899` requires an Intel E810-XXV-4T (Westport Channel) NIC with ≥3 PHC-sharing ports and a GNSS device; none of the lab workers (`cnfdf30/31/32`) satisfy these five constraints simultaneously, so `data.solutions["TBC"]` is always empty and `BeforeSuite` aborts before any spec can run.

- **11/36 failures — ts2phc stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suites: tgm)
  linuxptp-daemon PR #629 (SHA `14eb788`) injects `--servo_num_offset_values 10` into ts2phc CLI parameters in `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1120–1137`, requiring 10 consecutive offsets within threshold before declaring LOCKED. The E830 hardware in the CI lab cannot achieve 10 consecutive in-spec offsets with the dynamically computed `servo_offset_threshold`, so ts2phc remains in FREERUN despite `dpll=LOCKED`. This blocks ptp4l from reaching clock class 6 and phc2sys from locking, causing all 11 T-GM suite tests to fail.
